items.discussion: the owner's ruling on store-47's report, 2026-10-05
items.title: fixed-size arrays (`[T; n]`) implement `Items<T>`, so `list.push_many([1, 2, 3])` takes one
items.body: A158 landed `List::push_many(items)` over the new trait `std::iterator::Items<T>`, implemented by `List<T>`, `HashSet<T>` and every `Iterator<T>`. The owner accepted the trait's name and home (2026-10-05). Fixed-size arrays are not `Items`; this is the follow-up. Both backends, a pin in `inference::std_surface` beside `a158_*`, the native differential.

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (RULED by the owner on store-47's report; Order 48)
items.title: a struct literal that writes a std-`[internal]` field is refused outside std — `Store { root = .. }` still builds today, though reading the same field is refused since A149 S4
items.body: A149 S4 (store-47, Order 47) made a member READ of a field std marks `[internal]` a refusal outside std. Construction was outside the ruling and is still allowed. The owner ruled 2026-10-05, as the integrator recommended: refuse construction too, for consistency, with the same reason text (`labels::internal_field_out_of_reach` is the shared rule). Check destructuring patterns that name an internal field at the same time and say what they do. Breaking; count the estate (std, corpus, docs, examples, kolt, website) before the flip.

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (RULED by the owner on debug-47's report; Order 48 or a follow-up lane)
items.title: a written or derived `Debug` impl decides how `dbg` prints that type, and `[derive(Debug)]` spells enum variants qualified (`Shape::Circle(1.5)`), as the printer does
items.body: debug-47 built `dbg`'s generated printers and S4's `Debug` impls separately: a derived `Debug` prints `Circle(1.5)`, `dbg` prints `Shape::Circle(1.5)`. RULED 2026-10-05, as recommended: (1) a written `Debug` impl overrides how `dbg` prints that type; (2) the derive changes its spelling to the qualified form so the two agree; (3) `.debug()` stays opt-in through the derive, with no implicit bound on every type (`dbg` is the no-derive path). Both backends byte-identical; the committed `native/dbg_printer.stderr` moves with (2).

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (RULED by the owner on debug-47's report)
items.title: `dbg(-0.0)` prints `-0.0` — it prints `0.0` today under N136's `String(x)` rule; `print` keeps `0`
items.body: RULED 2026-10-05, as recommended: `dbg` is a debugging tool and shows the real value, so negative zero prints `-0.0` on both backends; `print` keeps N136's `0`. Pin beside `s1_dbg_writes_the_same_bytes_on_both_backends`.

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (RULED by the owner on debug-47's report)
items.title: `dbg`'s layout fills a list of scalars up to the 80-column limit, not one entry per line
items.body: debug-47's layout breaks any value past 80 columns one entry per line, so a long numeric list prints as a column. RULED 2026-10-05, as recommended: a list (and set) whose entries are all scalars fills each line to the limit; aggregates keep one entry per line. Both layout runtimes (`__dbg_layout`, `vilan_rt::show`) byte-identical; the 100-entry cap stands.

items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (RULED by the owner on debug-47's report: fix, do not accept the gap)
items.title: `print(x)` with `x: T` instantiated at a float is not wrapped, so negative zero can still print differently on JS and native inside a generic function — N136's recording is static
items.body: N136 (debug-47) wraps numeric `print` arguments in `String(x)` on JS from a static recording of the argument's type. A generic `T` grounded to `f64` per instance is not recorded. RULED 2026-10-05: fix it per instance (the emitter already emits per instantiation where the body differs; otherwise a runtime `typeof` check at the print site of an open-typed argument). Pin in the native differential with a generic function called at `f64` with `-0.0`.

items.body: class-writes.md (papers-47) RULED 2026-10-05 as recommended: writers stay last-wins and never append (Q1); the visible double write becomes an error at the next breaking cut (Q2; 0 sites across kolt, the website and the examples: 405 writers, none doubled); the warning's two gaps are fixed first (Q3: A159 `bind_attr`/`toggle_attr` on "class", A160 the wrong claim when the earlier writer is reactive); double writes across a function call stay silent with a census trigger and the append options stay parked (Q4); A155 closes on the paper (Q5). This item is the flip. Order: A159 + A160 in Order 48, the error at that order's cut.
